examples.solution_text:
Divide by the coefficient of $x$, which is $4$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int\dfrac{10}{4x+7}\,dx\\&=\dfrac{10}{4}\ln|4x+7|+C\\&=\dfrac{5}{2}\ln|4x+7|+C\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
Evaluate:

(a) $\int_{e}^{e^{3}}\dfrac{2}{x}\,dx$.

(b) $\int_{-7}^{-3}\dfrac{2}{x+1}\,dx$, giving an exact answer and a value correct to 4 significant figures.
examples.solution_text:
(a) The denominator is non-zero throughout the interval.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int_{e}^{e^{3}}\dfrac{2}{x}\,dx\\&=\left[2\ln|x|\right]_{e}^{e^{3}}\\&=2(3-1)\\&=4\end{aligned}$

(b) The denominator is zero at $x=-1$, outside $[-7,-3]$.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int_{-7}^{-3}\dfrac{2}{x+1}\,dx\\&=\left[2\ln|x+1|\right]_{-7}^{-3}\\&=2(\ln2-\ln6)\\&=-2\ln3\\&\approx-2.197\end{aligned}$

Split the fraction and integrate each term separately.

$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\int\dfrac{3x^{3}-4x+8}{x^{2}}\,dx\\&=\int\left(3x-\dfrac{4}{x}+8x^{-2}\right)\,dx\\&=\dfrac{3x^{2}}{2}-4\ln|x|+\dfrac{8x^{-1}}{-1}+C\\&=\dfrac{3x^{2}}{2}-4\ln|x|-\dfrac{8}{x}+C\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Given $f'(x)=2+\dfrac{8}{2x+3}$ for $x>-\dfrac{3}{2}$ and $f(-1)=1$, find $f(x)$ and hence $f(1)$.
Find the exact value of $a$, where $a<0$, if $\int_{a}^{-3}\dfrac{2}{x}\,dx=4$.
examples.solution_text:
Since $a<0$, the interval stays on the negative side of $x=0$.

$\begin{aligned}2\left[\ln|x|\right]_{a}^{-3}&=4\\2(\ln3-\ln|a|)&=4\\\ln3-\ln|a|&=2\\\ln|a|&=\ln3-2\\|a|&=3e^{-2}\end{aligned}$

Since $a<0$, $a=-3e^{-2}$.

$\begin{aligned}2x-6&=0\\x&=3\end{aligned}$

The denominator is zero at $x=3$, inside $[0,5]$. The integral is undefined; substituting the limits into a logarithmic primitive is not valid.

examples.derivation: The denominator derivative is 4, so the primitive is (10/4)ln|4x+7|+C = (5/2)ln|4x+7|+C. Its derivative is 10/(4x+7).
The denominator derivative is −6. Multiplying ln|5−6x| by 8/(−6) gives −(4/3)ln|5−6x|+C, whose derivative is 8/(5−6x).
(a) 2[ln|x|] from e to e³ gives 2(3−1)=4. (b) The pole −1 is outside [−7,−3]; endpoint substitution gives 2(ln2−ln6)=−2ln3≈−2.197224577, hence −2.197 to four significant figures.
Division gives 3x−4/x+8x⁻². Termwise integration gives 3x²/2−4ln|x|−8/x+C. Differentiation reproduces all three terms.
Integration gives f(x)=2x+4ln|2x+3|+C. At x=−1, −2+4ln1+C=1, so C=3. Thus f(1)=2+4ln5+3=5+4ln5. The stated domain contains both evaluation points and excludes the pole.
Both limits are negative, so the integration interval excludes zero. The equation is 2(ln3−ln|a|)=4, giving |a|=3e⁻² and a=−3e⁻². Substitution gives 2(ln3−(ln3−2))=4; reversed limit order is valid.
Solving 2x−6=0 gives x=3, strictly inside [0,5]. The integrand has a non-removable pole there, so the definite integral is undefined.
